clue.text: Do I act wrongly in exposing Indian robber?

indicators.note: doing something wrongly means doing it out of order, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they are acting badly in unmasking a bandit from India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' rearranges DOIACT (the letters of 'Do I act'). A DACOIT was a member of an armed robber gang in India and Burma.
explanation.definitionFit: The word comes from Hindi and names a bandit belonging to an armed gang.

clue.text: Resistance from French bridegroom-to-be

parts.note: de is the French word for from
a man engaged to be married is a fiancé

explanation.surface: Opposition comes from a Frenchman about to marry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' looks like a link; with 'French' it gives the French word DE.
explanation.definitionFit: Open refusal to obey or yield is a form of opposition.

clue.text: Opportunity given to apprentice in church

parts.note: a chance is an opportunity
L stands for learner, an apprentice, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A trainee gets a lucky break working for the church.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the part of a church near the altar, reserved for clergy and choir.

clue.text: Such a policy guarantees security

parts.note: the whole clue describes cover bought from an underwriter, a policy that protects against loss

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain kind of policy keeps one safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'policy' sounds like a government plan; it is the document an insurer issues.
explanation.definitionFit: Cover paid for against loss or damage is protection, a form of financial safety.

clue.text: Put up fight on being discarded

explanation.surface: Someone resisted when they were thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrap is both to brawl, so a fighter has scrapped, and to throw away as useless, so junk is scrapped.

clue.text: Diligence Alan's displayed to get domestics

indicators.note: displayed suggests the letters are spread out and set out afresh, rearranged

explanation.surface: Alan shows such diligence that he is rewarded with servants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displayed' rearranges the fourteen letters of 'Diligence Alan's', including the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Domestics are household servants, such as women employed to clean homes.

clue.text: Stop at sea to collect a huge following

parts.note: vast means huge

explanation.surface: A large crowd of followers is gathered by someone told to stop at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor's command to halt or cease, used aboard ship.

clue.text: Relate to avant-garde painter

indicators.note: avant-garde means unconventional and experimental, so the letters of painter are rearranged

explanation.surface: A link is drawn to an experimental painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avant-garde' looks like a description of the painter but rearranges its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To pertain to something is to concern it or have a bearing on it, to relate to it.

clue.text: Melodious two-part song about lake and castle

indicators.note: about means the song for two goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a duet is a song for two voices
L is the map abbreviation for lake
C is the chess notation abbreviation for castle

explanation.surface: A tuneful duet is sung about a lake and a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A dulcet sound is sweet and soothing to hear, as a tuneful one is.

clue.text: Overseas amours embassies are concerned with

explanation.surface: Diplomats deal with romances conducted abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Love affairs abroad are, punningly, affairs that are foreign, while the phrase also names the international relations diplomats handle.

clue.text: Iris needs 14 pounds to get paving

parts.note: the yellow flag is a wild iris, so a flag is a kind of iris
a stone is a British weight of fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: A gardener's iris needs a heavy weight to make a path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iris' looks like a woman's name; it is the flower. A STONE is the British unit of weight, 14 pounds, still used for body weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A large flat slab used to pave a path or floor is called by this name.

clue.text: A couple I left in springtime

parts.note: PR is the abbreviation for pair, a couple

explanation.surface: Two people and I set off in the spring.
explanation.definitionFit: This month falls in spring in the northern hemisphere, so it stands for the season.

clue.text: Russian leader put in charge? Damn!

indicators.note: the leader is put into the middle of the word for charge, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to charge someone with a crime is to accuse them

indicators.note: the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the leading letter of Russian is R

explanation.surface: A Russian is appointed to head things, and someone curses at the news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Russian leader' gives only R, the word's first letter, not a Kremlin figure.
explanation.definitionFit: To curse someone is to call down damnation on them, an old-fashioned verb.

clue.text: He's mad to bring an action against teachers

indicators.note: against means next to, so the teachers' union stands alongside the lawsuit

parts.note: NUT is the National Union of Teachers, a British trade union
an action at law is a case

explanation.surface: Someone is crazy enough to sue the schoolteachers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'against' looks like opposition in a lawsuit, but it only places one piece beside the other. The NUT was the main British teachers' union.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackpot or lunatic is informally called this, so 'he's mad' describes one.

clue.text: Look into swindle in Panama

indicators.note: into means the word for look is put inside the word for swindle

parts.note: a con is a swindle or confidence trick
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Investigators examine a fraud in Panama.
explanation.definitionFit: Colón is a port city at the Caribbean end of the canal in that Central American country.

clue.text: Traps heather into taking alcoholic drink

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap for game, so traps are gins
ling is the common heather of moorland

explanation.surface: Snares catch on moorland heather while someone drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: LING is the common heather of British moors.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin sling is a cocktail of gin, sweetened water and lemon.

clue.text: Many sentries become radio enthusiasts

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, crossword shorthand for many

indicators.note: become means the letters of sentries change into something new

explanation.surface: Many guards turn into fans of the wireless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' looks like a quantity of guards; it is L, fifty in Roman numerals. 'become' signals that the letters of 'sentries' are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: People who tune in to radio programmes are its audience, those who hear it.

clue.text: As lively as a séance, maybe

explanation.surface: Someone is as animated as a gathering to contact the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means full of energy, and punningly describes a séance, an event attended by ghosts.

clue.text: Bottom of the pile despite expectations

explanation.surface: Someone at the bottom of the heap ended up there against all expectations.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming behind everyone is being last of the lot, while the phrase also means nevertheless, contrary to what was anticipated.

clue.text: Film documenting era of imperial rule

parts.note: a foot is an imperial measure, the length of a standard ruler
an age is an era

explanation.surface: A documentary covering a period of empire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imperial rule' looks like the government of an empire; it is the twelve-inch ruler of imperial measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Recorded film material is measured and sold by length, hence the name for it.

clue.text: Street music with beat

parts.note: rap is a style of music

explanation.surface: Street music that has a strong rhythm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat' looks like a musical rhythm to go with the street music; it is the verb to thrash.
explanation.definitionFit: To strap someone is to thrash them with a leather belt, as punishment.

clue.text: Violent action from a member in fury

indicators.note: in means the article and the member go inside the word for fury

parts.note: rage is fury
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A violent outburst from a furious politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A rampage is a spell of wild, destructive behaviour.

clue.text: Help to ensure a ship is on time

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Advice to make sure a vessel sails punctually.
explanation.definitionFit: To aid or support someone is to give them help.

clue.text: Draw attention to "Chicago"'s closure!

parts.note: Chicago is a famous stage musical, so it is a show
a show that closes is off, taken off the stage

explanation.surface: An exclamation urging people to notice that the musical Chicago is closing.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'Chicago' the musical rather than the city.
explanation.definitionFit: To flaunt or parade something is to display it so others notice it.

clue.text: In Dover the asylum seekers are visible

indicators.note: in means the letters lie inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Migrants arriving at Dover can be clearly seen.
explanation.walkthrough: Dover is the English Channel port where many asylum seekers land.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overt is out in the open, plainly seen and not hidden.

clue.text: He has visions of me in drab accommodation

indicators.note: in, with accommodation, means the word me is housed inside the word for drab

parts.note: drear is a poetic word for dull or drab

explanation.surface: Someone imagines the speaker living in dreary lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sees things in sleep or imagines ideals is this kind of person.

clue.text: I reckon it means "enraged"

parts.note: to rate something is to reckon or judge it

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a word means furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone very angry; the answer is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Get a linen outfit that's far from chic

indicators.note: outfit read as a verb means the letters are kitted out anew, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to buy a linen suit that is not at all stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outfit' looks like clothing; it rearranges GETALINEN (the letters of 'Get a linen').
explanation.definitionFit: Something clumsy or lacking grace and style is the opposite of chic.

clue.text: Doctor is initially eager to publish paper

parts.note: to doctor a patient is to treat them

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of eager is used

explanation.surface: A physician is keen to get an article published.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a noun, a physician; it is the verb meaning to treat.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper can be a scholarly essay, a formal written study of a subject.

clue.text: East German objective is channel port

parts.note: Ost is the German word for east
an end is an aim or objective

explanation.surface: An East German's goal is a port on the Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East German' looks like a person from the old GDR; it means the German word for east.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostend is a Belgian ferry port facing England across the water.
